title: Flagpost import-code resolution response
description: The body returned by GET {marketplace_url}/resolve/{code}. It carries everything the instance needs to render the install confirmation/trust screen and then fetch + verify the artifact (draft: ADR-0040, docs/MODULES.md §5.2). The code is a LOOKUP KEY, never the trust boundary — the instance MUST independently re-verify signature, digest, and compatibility locally before installing, and MUST NOT trust the `compatible`/`trust` booleans here as anything more than a display hint.

code.description: The code that was resolved, echoed back.

capabilities.description: Capabilities the module requests — rendered as the consent list. Authoritative copy lives in the signed artifact's manifest; the instance re-reads it after download and refuses if the download asks for more than was consented to.

permissions.description: RBAC permission keys the module would add on install (code tier) — shown for consent.

compatible.description: The registry's view of whether this artifact fits the requesting instance's version (if the instance sent one). A DISPLAY HINT ONLY — the instance re-checks requires_flagpost against its own version.

trust.description: The registry's assertions about provenance — all DISPLAY HINTS. The instance re-derives real trust by verifying the signature against its own policy/keystore.

official.description: Signed by the Flagpost project root key (first-party).

commerce.description: Present when the artifact is paid or entitlement-gated. The entitlement is checked at DOWNLOAD time and thereafter verified OFFLINE — there is no runtime license phone-home (docs/MODULES.md §7).

entitlement_present.description: Whether the resolution was made with a valid entitlement (e.g. the code was itself a purchase token, or an account entitlement was presented). If false and entitlement_required is true, the instance shows obtain_url instead of an install button.

obtain_url.description: Where a human buys/obtains the entitlement (opened in the operator's browser, never called by the server).

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 time after which this resolution (and any short-lived signed artifact URL in it) is stale and must be re-resolved.
